method: commands per poll: lib/run/poll-cost.ts, the real RedisShopStore, limiter and snapshot code on an in-memory Redis that counts every command (a call is 1, each pipelined command is 1; an EVAL is 1), 20 polls of a 3-order session. Polls per 10 minutes: the lane's own pollDelayMs replayed on a timeline (a model, not a measured session). Nothing was sent to Redis or PayPal. The server's own count (an EVAL counts the commands inside it) is not re-measured here: docs/measurements/s5-poll-cost.json has 6.35 per poll on the real database (10-19).

idle.note: a session is opened and nothing is done; the tab stays open and visible

active.note: a visit in the judge's five steps (model timeline below), then quiet until minute 10

snapshots.what: the order is placed: the books are given time to settle
the payment event is heard and the shop booked it
the refund is asked for: the row is too new to call
the refund event is heard; the shop answered 200 and booked nothing
the gap is found; PayPal has not listed the refund event yet
PayPal lists the event: Ring again is on, the judge's turn
Ring again: the resend is on its way
the resend arrived; the books are checked

criterion.problem: A13 item 9 says 'at most 60 Redis commands per session per 10 minutes'. One poll is 7 commands, so 60 is 8 polls. A lane that is waiting for PayPal (its event list takes 80 to 163 s, its own retries about 163 s) polls every 5 to 20 s, which is 10 to 30 polls in those minutes: 60 cannot hold for a session that does anything, whatever the pace, without the page going stale.
criterion.kept: an idle session (open, nothing done) costs at most 60 in 10 minutes: 49 now, 224 before
criterion.proposal: Keep 60 for an idle session. For a session that is used, replace it with (a) one poll is at most 7 commands, pinned by lib/run/poll-cost.test.ts, and (b) the hourly caps already in lib/limits.ts: 300 polls per session per hour (2,100 commands) and 600 for all sessions (4,200 commands). The modelled five-step visit costs about 270 commands in its 10 minutes, and a judge's visit is one such session. The owner decides.
criterion.notDone: Reading less per poll (a version counter written by every write, read first by the poll) would cut an unchanged poll to 2 or 3 commands, but the waits are on PayPal's clock, which no Redis key shows, so the full scan would still run every 5 to 20 s while a gap waits. It changes the store's layout and is not done here.

fitsInPlan.note: 60 commands is 8 polls. The idle lane makes 7. An active visit needs the lane to poll while PayPal's clock is awaited, which is many more than 8; no pace keeps that inside 60 without making the page unusable (lib/limits.ts says the same). See criterion.
